messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service: nightly-batches (service id: svc_89ab). Priority: P1. Trigger: job-scheduler timeout > 5m. Link: https://pd/reports/INC-2771234567 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: escalation: primary (infra-oncall) not ACKED -> paging rotation -> infra-dev (rotation: infra-dev-night)
mike: seeing a ton of pages. did we just wake the whole infra-dev team?
jessie: yes. I'm getting 8 duplicate pages in the last 2 mins.
incident-bot: note: schedule override applied 01:30 UTC today by automation: nightly-override-sync (reason: calendar sync). Affected binding: svc_89ab currently points to infra-dev-night (expected: sre-night).
sara: wait, expected oncall is sre-night. who applied that override?
devops: that was from automated schedule drift fixer. it incorrectly matched tag "infra" on the service.
mike: ohhh the tagging rule. svc_89ab has tag=infra because of old metadata.
ops-lead: immediate ask: stop paging, rebind service to correct schedule, and notify infra-dev to quiet the channel.
jessie: trying an emergency mute on PagerDuty for svc_89ab -> muting vendor alert channel (will still escalate to managers).
pagerduty-bot: mute applied to svc_89ab for 15m by jessie. escalation still active for existing pages.
devops: running PD CLI to change the service binding: pd service-binding update svc_89ab --schedule sre-night --from automation.
(devops pasted code block)
```
# pd cli
pd service-binding update svc_89ab --schedule sre-night --reason "rollback wrong override 01:30"
```

mike: +1 executing. please confirm when live.
incident-bot: note: manual acknowledgement from infra-dev user alicia at 2771234620 (ack all current pages).
sara: alicia acked but she says her team wasn't responsible and left the channel. we're at risk of missed pages if we rely on ack. need routing fix instead.
devops: update succeeded. new binding: svc_89ab -> sre-night. PD propagation estimate 20s.
pagerduty-bot: binding change propagated. new page targets: sre-night (rotation id: rot_334). next escalation will route to sre-night-primary.
jessie: asking sre-night to confirm they got the page (cc @sre-night).
ops-lead: @sre-night please ACK if you see any alerts. also please check for missed customer-facing backfills.
(20s later) incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert for svc_89ab acknowledged by user ben (sre-night). Incident state: acknowledged.
mike: ben ACKed. can we confirm customer impact? logs show the nightly job timed out and restarted a shard. customer-facing jobs queued but 95% recovered within 3m, a few retries caused increased latency for model uploads between 01:25-01:40 UTC.
sara: I'm pulling metrics. Retention job consumer errors spiked x3. SLO for ingestion latency breached for 14 minutes. Customer impact: some uploads delayed -> ~120 customers saw >30s upload times. No data loss.
jessie: putting a temporary post on status.redwood: "Delayed nightly processing for some uploads; mitigation in progress."
ops-lead: good. follow-up actions: 1) revert faulty automation rule; 2) add test for tag-matching in override job; 3) run replay to catch missed jobs; 4) postmortem. Assign owners: devops for 1&2, eng-runtime for 3, product for comms.
devops: noted. disabling the nightly-override-sync job now and creating ticket RDW-4567.
mike: also recommend adding a guard in routing: explicit service-id whitelist when automation runs.
sara: logging the names/ids of affected customers and sending targeted emails tomorrow.
ops-lead: closing the paging noise. final note: incident essentially mitigated by rebinding PD service and mute. create incident follow-up doc and put in "incidents/ongoing".
jessie: will schedule postmortem 48h out and include small blameless section. any objections?
mike: none. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for paging storm but keep channel open for follow-ups."
